scoring: acceptable = events the owner would show (counts for recall and precision). secondary = lower-confidence picks: fine to show (not a precision miss) but not required (no recall credit). not_good = would not show (precision miss, not a blocking gate). forbidden = must never show (blocking).

forbidden_everywhere.notes: Owner, 2026-11-19: closure notices are not events. Showing one for any question is a blocking failure; the screen should say Nothing matched instead.

duplicate_groups.rule: Owner, 2026-11-19: show one card per program. In scoring, events with the same title in the same question count as one group: citing either copy earns full credit, and citing two copies of one program is not required.

design_decisions: One card per program (avoid near-duplicates) unless the parent asked for that specific program.
A general question with no category (e.g. something for my 4-year-old) gets a varied mix, framed like: Here are a variety of things you could do...
Unsupported city: say Nothing matched. Open Eventz covers Frisco and Plano only, then offer up to 5 varied events from the tab city on those dates.
LIBRARY CLOSED notices must never be shown; show Nothing matched instead.
parse_expectations: Dates, city, free and age are read from the question wording; the owner accepted Claude's reading (labels.json expect fields) and did not change any. The owner's picks are consistent with them (e.g. Q9 includes Dec 2).
